title: Degenerate queue snowball analysis and circuit-breaker implementation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Post-incident follow-up for a hosted API GPU exhaustion event that created a self-reinforcing queue growth pattern. This ticket captures the analysis, short-term mitigations deployed, and the design + rollout plan for a tenant-level circuit breaker and admission guard to prevent recurrence.
impact: Hosted API experienced sustained request queue growth across three GPU pools for ~22 minutes. Median tail latency increased 3.2x for affected tenants and overall token throughput dropped by ~28% while GPU utilization oscillated between 40-95% due to short-lived KV cache pressure and batch packing inefficiencies.
timeline: 2026-01-31 14:03 UTC — first alert: per-pool queued_requests metric exceeded 8K
2026-01-31 14:05 UTC — autoscaler started scale-up, observed high provisioning lag (2.5m) from cloud side
2026-01-31 14:07 UTC — several large tenants submitted prefetch/bursty multi-request patterns; KV cache hit-rate dropped 18%
2026-01-31 14:10 UTC — admission controller allowed many long-seq requests; per-request GPU memory increased leading to concurrent slot reduction
2026-01-31 14:21 UTC — operator-run throttle applied to top-10 noisy tenants and manual prewarm invoked; queue began slow drain
2026-01-31 14:40 UTC — system returned to baseline over next 30 minutes with manual interventions and draining policies
root_cause: A compound failure: bursty tenant prefetch + a KV cache pollution regression increased per-request GPU memory resulting in reduced packing density. The autoscaler had conservative hysteresis and relied on cloud provisioning that introduced multi-minute node start lag. The admission controller lacked a tenant-scoped circuit breaker, enabling a small set of noisy tenants to amplify queue length and delay recovery.
mitigations_deployed: Triage: temporary rate-limits applied to the 12 top contributors to queued requests (operator action)
Short-term config: lower per-tenant prefetch default from 8 to 3 for hosted-only tenants (config roll)
Hotfix: reverted KV cache aggressive eviction heuristics from earlier rollout (runtime PR 1245)
Operational: prewarm job run for affected pools and added automated alert to trigger prewarm when queued_requests > 2k
analysis_notes: Observed a 22% reduction in average tokens-per-packet packing during the incident window — packing inefficiency accounted for ~12% of throughput loss
Top 5 tenants accounted for 63% of the sustained queue growth; one tenant sent repeated long-context generation chains without respecting backpressure guidance
Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts aborted due to instance launch quota throttle in region us-west-2 resulting in provisioning delays
The admission controller lacked per-tenant soft-fail thresholds (we had only global thresholds)
KV cache regression introduced more cold-cache kernels causing slower per-token latency and transient memory spikes

design_decisions: Circuit breaker semantics: two-stage (soft backpressure threshold -> delayed admission -> hard reject above emergency threshold) to prefer degradation over total outage
Tenant scoring will consider recent queue contribution, average request length, KV cache miss-rate, and historical rate-limit infractions
Fallback model routing: when circuit breaker trips, route to a smaller compatible model variant if available (configurable per customer)
Expose 'circuit-breaker' hints in Console with explainability and estimated impact before enabling for a tenant
implementation_plan: Week 1: landing design doc and API contract for admission controller changes (runtime and control-plane) — PRs: runtime #1302, control-plane #714
Week 2: implement soft-limit evaluation and per-tenant sliding window accounting; add telemetry for decisions
Week 3: deploy to canary pools, exercise with synthetic-burst test, collect metrics for false positives
Week 4: gradual rollout to hosted pools with auto-rollout gates based on false-positive rate < 0.5% and recovery time improvement > 30%

follow_up_notes: We expect the combination of tenant circuit-breaker + faster prewarm to reduce mean recovery time by >40% in simulated bursts
Monitor for false positives during canary and be prepared to relax soft thresholds quickly
This incident highlights the need for per-tenant observability; next quarter roadmap should include tenant heatmaps and 'noisy neighbor' alerts
